text:
Anya: thinking out loud — can we add a routing-decision playback to the Trace view that shows the exact policy checks + model-variant fallback path for a request? need something we can hand to support and SREs :thinking_face:
Tom: yes. lightweight view first: show final decision, list of rule matches, and the headers that influenced it. expandable nodes for details. :white_check_mark:
Priya: +1. also want a delta view: which rule caused a fallback (e.g., capacity vs tier policy). super helpful when a premium customer got routed to a cheaper variant.
Matt: caution: exposing headers means customer_id, org, maybe other PII. we should strip or hash identifiers before showing in console by default.
Anya: agree on PII. minimal: show tier (e.g., "premium"/"standard"), region, and model_family, and an obfuscated org id. full headers behind a gated "show raw" button with audit log.
Olga: UX idea — show a small decision graph: start -> policy checks (quota, region, tier) -> variant selection (preferred model -> fallback model) -> final node with latency/cost estimate. each node clickable to open telemetry queries.
Tom: implementation note: we can emit a compact routing trace proto per request with fields: policy_ids[], reasons[], selected_variant, candidate_variants[], route_headers. keep it tiny (50-200 bytes typically). store sampled traces in TSDB/backing store.
Priya: sampling config needs to be configurable per org and per route. for high-impact customers we want 100% sampling for 24h on-demand. telemetry-bot can flip a flag temporarily.
telemetry-bot: note — current default sampling = 0.1% globally, can be raised to 100% per-org via /telemetry ramp. logs retained 14d by default.
Matt: audit + retention policy: we should make retention configurable per workspace and surface costs prominently. and ensure routing-traces are excluded from analytics exports unless explicitly enabled.
Anya: question about header surface: should we encode routing metadata into an outgoing header so downstream services can show the same decision context? e.g., `x-redwood-routing: tier=premium;model=redwood-1.2-quant;reason=capacity-fallback;region=eu-west-1`
Tom: +1 for a small header. benefits: easier debugging across services, quicker correlation in logs. downside: we might leak internal variant names to customer logs if they proxy responses. maybe base64 or tokenized header referencing server-side trace id.
Olga: UX for console: add a filter bar: tenant, route, timeframe, decision-reason (capacity|quota|latency_penalty), selected-variant, fallback-depth. also a column showing cost delta if fallback used (approx tokens * cost diff).
Priya: also add a "replay" button that replays the decision path on a dev-only sandbox (no real tokens charged) so engineers can reproduce. gated by perms.
Matt: API debate: should we return routing decision in API response body for internal customers (e.g., dedicated) vs only in console? returning in body helps infra integrations but is a breaking surface. prefer header or trace_id only.
Tom: proposed: API response includes `x-rd-trace-id` + `x-rd-routing-hash` (non-PII) for everyone. detailed decoded decision available via console or internal API with proper auth. that avoids expanding the public contract.
Anya: logging/telemetry: add a dashboard panel that correlates fallback rate by customer tier and region. alert if premium fallback_rate > 1% in last 1h. show owners.
telemetry-bot: created issue #PLAT-789 to add fallback_rate metric and alert. sampling knobs tracked in #PLAT-790.
Olga: we should add a visual diff when a rollout changes default variant for a route: show before/after expected latency and cost, and simulated fallback scenarios. helpful during canaries.
Priya: +1 for simulation. can we run a quick batch job that replays last N requests against the new policy and surface failures/extra fallbacks?
Tom: doable. need to be careful about replaying user data — scrub PII and run in a safe sandbox.
Matt: final callouts: ensure RBAC around "show raw headers" and "replay"; default to obfuscation and short retention; surface cost to customer-facing dashboards so support can explain why fallback happened.
Anya: ok next steps: Tom to spec the routing-trace proto + minimal header proposal, Priya to spec sampling/retention UX, Olga to mock the trace UI, Matt to write privacy/RBAC guardrails. will sync in a 30m design review.
Tom: I'll drop the proto draft and header examples here in ~1h.
Anya: thanks all — this will make debugging and support much faster :raised_hands:
